title: Direct and indirect objects
subtitle: Verbs with no object, one object, or two objects

blocks.text: Some verbs only need a subject. They don't need an object.
Many verbs can be followed by an object.

rows.example: We picked up **the rubbish**. I've planted **a tree**.

blocks.text: Some verbs can be followed by two objects. One is the **direct object** and the other is the **indirect object**. The indirect object is usually a person. In **Simon gave Jill some flowers**, **some flowers** is the direct object and **Jill** is the indirect object.

rows.use: subject + verb + indirect object + direct object
subject + verb + direct object + preposition + indirect object

blocks.intro: There are two prepositions which often go between the direct object and the indirect object: **to** and **for**.
Some of the verbs above can also be used in the passive.

blocks.text: We don't use a preposition if the indirect object comes before the direct object.

exercises.title: A · Match the objects
exercises.instruction: Choose the phrase that completes each sentence. If the verb cannot take an object, choose X.

items.prompt: I've never driven
acceptedAnswers: a tractor.

items.prompt: We're going to have
acceptedAnswers: a party on Saturday.

items.prompt: Don't close
acceptedAnswers: the window!

items.prompt: Have you invited
acceptedAnswers: lots of people?

items.prompt: Our rabbit has run away
acceptedAnswers: X (no object)

items.prompt: Of course you can borrow
acceptedAnswers: some money.

items.prompt: Clare has drawn
acceptedAnswers: a lovely picture.

items.prompt: I think I'll sit down
acceptedAnswers: X (no object)

exercises.title: B · Extra word
exercises.instruction: Write the extra word in each sentence.

items.prompt: My mum often **makes for** the old lady who lives next door some soup.
acceptedAnswers: for

items.prompt: I won't **tell to** anyone your secret.
acceptedAnswers: to

items.prompt: **Sing to** us a song!
acceptedAnswers: to

items.prompt: Could you **bring for** me some crisps when you come?
acceptedAnswers: for

items.prompt: I think I'll **buy for** Carl a computer game for his birthday.
acceptedAnswers: for

items.prompt: That CD **cost to** me fifteen euros.
acceptedAnswers: to

items.prompt: Dan **showed to** me his autograph book.
acceptedAnswers: to

exercises.title: C · Direct object at the end
exercises.instruction: Rewrite the sentences with the direct object at the end.

items.prompt: I owe ten euros to Danny.
acceptedAnswers: I owe Danny ten euros.
I owe Danny ten euros

items.prompt: Susan hasn't bought a birthday present for her mum yet.
acceptedAnswers: Susan hasn't bought her mum a birthday present yet.
Susan hasn't bought her mum a birthday present yet
Susan has not bought her mum a birthday present yet.

items.prompt: You should show your new guitar to Mike.
acceptedAnswers: You should show Mike your new guitar.
You should show Mike your new guitar

items.prompt: Did you give that CD to Liz?
acceptedAnswers: Did you give Liz that CD?
Did you give Liz that CD

items.prompt: I'd like to teach English to young teenagers.
acceptedAnswers: I'd like to teach young teenagers English.
I'd like to teach young teenagers English
I would like to teach young teenagers English.

items.prompt: Are you going to write a letter to your grandparents?
acceptedAnswers: Are you going to write your grandparents a letter?
Are you going to write your grandparents a letter

items.prompt: Could you take this magazine to your dad?
acceptedAnswers: Could you take your dad this magazine?
Could you take your dad this magazine

exercises.title: D · Indirect object at the end
exercises.instruction: Rewrite the sentences with the indirect object at the end.

items.prompt: I'm going to read the kids a story.
acceptedAnswers: I'm going to read a story to the kids.
I'm going to read a story to the kids
I am going to read a story to the kids.

items.prompt: Could you pass Ed the potatoes?
acceptedAnswers: Could you pass the potatoes to Ed?
Could you pass the potatoes to Ed

items.prompt: Throw the dog that bone!
acceptedAnswers: Throw that bone to the dog!
Throw that bone to the dog
Throw that bone to the dog.

items.prompt: Why are you sending Aunty June those clothes?
acceptedAnswers: Why are you sending those clothes to Aunty June?
Why are you sending those clothes to Aunty June

items.prompt: Steve sang us his new song.
acceptedAnswers: Steve sang his new song to us.
Steve sang his new song to us

items.prompt: I'll lend Doug the money.
acceptedAnswers: I'll lend the money to Doug.
I'll lend the money to Doug
I will lend the money to Doug.

items.prompt: I've never told my mum a lie.
acceptedAnswers: I've never told a lie to my mum.
I've never told a lie to my mum
I have never told a lie to my mum.

exercises.title: E · to, for or dash
exercises.instruction: Write one word in each gap. If no word is necessary, put a dash (-).

items.prompt: My mum is going to write a letter ___ the editor.
acceptedAnswers: to

items.prompt: I paid the money ___ the shop assistant and then left.
acceptedAnswers: to

items.prompt: Let's get a birthday card ___ your dad.
acceptedAnswers: for

items.prompt: I'm not going to tell ___ you the answer!
I've made some sandwiches ___ Jake.
acceptedAnswers: for

items.prompt: We'll bring ___ you that DVD tonight.
Tony has bought a book ___ you.
acceptedAnswers: for

items.prompt: A prize was given ___ the best student.
acceptedAnswers: to

exercises.title: F · My new hobby
exercises.instruction: If the line is correct, write a dash (-). If there is an extra word, write that word.

items.prompt: My aunt recently **bought for** him a new telescope for his birthday.
acceptedAnswers: for

items.prompt: so he gave his old one to me! It's a very good telescope.
acceptedAnswers: correct

items.prompt: When he bought it, it **cost to** him over two hundred euros!
acceptedAnswers: to

items.prompt: Last weekend, he **taught to** me the basics.
acceptedAnswers: to

items.prompt: He showed me how to look through it, and **told to** me the names of all the planets.
acceptedAnswers: to

items.prompt: He said he'll **bring to** me a book with more information about the night sky next time he comes.
acceptedAnswers: to

items.prompt: Now astronomy is my hobby too. I think I'm going to enjoy it!
acceptedAnswers: correct
